questions.title: Exact replication and audit of the JSS beta-regression R example
questions.description: Conduct an L1 exact public-source replication of Francisco Cribari-Neto and Achim Zeileis's 2010 Journal of Statistical Software article, Beta Regression in R. Use only the operator-supplied hash-bound journal and historical-package source snapshot and the operator-pinned execution. Inspect the article text, provenance record, unmodified official R example, environment lock and probe, historical betareg and Formula metadata and source, and the supplied data documentation. Run the pinned journal source once with no editing, wrapper, replacement implementation, model-authored argument, or network access. In one durable Markdown report, identify the article, DOI, official PDF and R-source identities, historical package archives, source snapshot, exact entrypoint and command, interpreter, package versions, and successful source-integrity checks. Reconstruct the script's execution order and account for every printed analysis: the fixed-dispersion GasolineYield fit and observation-omission precision comparison; the FoodExpenditure OLS heteroskedasticity diagnostic; the variable-dispersion GasolineYield and FoodExpenditure likelihood-ratio comparisons and information-criterion output; the pseudo-R-squared, link, RESET-type, convergence, and FoodExpenditure log-likelihood comparisons; and the ReadingSkills OLS and variable-dispersion beta-regression coefficient tests. Interpret every reported statistic and p value at its stated threshold without converting non-rejection into evidence for a null, selecting a universally best link or dispersion model from one dataset, or making causal, package-wide, theoretical, or novelty claims. Account for all source plot-producing stages and the declared Rplots.pdf artifact, while distinguishing source-derived expectations and artifact metadata from visual or pixel-level inspection. Explain that the structural-change section generates seeded artificial data and graphical fluctuation-process output but prints no test verdict in this run. Distinguish this current R 4.4.3 execution with historical betareg 2.2-0 and Formula 1.0-0 from reconstruction of the authors' full 2010 operating system, R, BLAS, graphics device, dependency stack, every article result, or raw-PDF byte identity across reruns. No model-authored estimator, replacement simulation, new theorem, novelty claim, or Lean formalization is required. Disclose all remaining source, version, environment, numerical, visualization, inferential, and scientific-scope gaps honestly.
